chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUdhāfir, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the time of Maghrib, and he said: If it is more gentle for you and more feasible for you in your salat (prayer), and you are occupied with your needs, then you may delay it until a quarter of the night.
He said: He said this to me while he was present in his town.

key_terms.أَرْفَقَ بِكَ: more gentle or easier for you
key_terms.أَمْكَنَ لَكَ: more practicable or manageable for you
key_terms.وَقْتِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the prescribed time of the Maghrib salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Until what time may Maghrib salat (prayer) be delayed according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the timing of Maghrib salat (prayer) and indicates that delaying it is permitted when doing so is easier and more manageable, especially when one is occupied with personal needs. It reflects a legal ruling in Shia fiqh that allows flexibility in the time of Maghrib up to a quarter of the night under such circumstances.
